# Chemical stocks: how to analyze chemical companies

**Chemical stocks are shares in companies refining raw materials into molecules — a sector with two very different economies: bulk chemicals, where profit is rented from the gas price year by year, and specialty chemicals, where the formula and its approvals own the margin for decades.** [The course on the chemical sector](/kurser/se-21-kemisektorn) calls the industry finance's third half — the sector series' most global: AK1A's universe holds six carriers on six exchanges in six countries — Yara, BASF, Sherwin-Williams, Air Liquide, Nutrien, Shin-Etsu — with no large Swedish chemical company listed, the global reading is the norm.

## The industry's two worlds — bulk chemicals versus specialty chemicals

The sector's most important curve is not a price chart but a classification. Bulk sells molecules — ammonia, urea, methanol, plastic granulate — millions of tonnes of identical products, buyers switching supplier for a one-krona difference: gross margin roughly 12 to 18 percent, price set by the world's supply ladder. Specialty sells what bulk cannot: an exact specification, an approval in the customer's process, a formula taking years to develop and replace — margin band around 25 to 40 percent. The course's invented contrast companies show it: Norden Bulk: revenue 12,000 million kronor at 18 percent gross margin — 12,000 × 18 percent = 2,160 million gross profit; Norden Special: revenue 3,000 at 38 percent — 3,000 × 38 percent = 1,140. Specialty carries 34.5 percent of the pair's gross profit on 20 percent of revenue. Same label, two economies: the same P/E means different things in a gas-bill and a formula business. Read the margin with [the gross margin ratio](/kurser/v07-bruttomarginal) and the moat with [the birth of the moat](/kurser/mt-04-vallgravens-fodelse): one number, two origins.

## The gas bill — raw-material leverage in chemical stocks

The air is 78 percent nitrogen — free to take; energy is what costs. Ammonia synthesis, industrialized in 1913, requires about 33 energy units per tonne — the arithmetic is multiplication. At 4 dollars per unit, gas cost is 33 × 4 = 132 dollars per tonne; at 8, 264; at 12, 396. Every gas-price dollar is 33 dollars per tonne — same factory, same molecule, three profitability worlds. In the 2021 to 2022 energy crisis, European gas became many times more expensive than North American and nitrogen plants halted — [the energy price as macro phenomenon](/kurser/km-043-energisektorn) is the energy course's; this guide owns its path through the income statement. The universe's witness is Yara: revenue fell from 249.7 to 165.1 billion Norwegian kronor between fiscal 2022 and 2023 (minus 33.9 percent), earnings from 28.8 billion 2022 via 510 million 2023 to 157 million 2024 — 0.5 percent of the peak year, before recovery to 13.0 billion 2025, 45 percent of the top. [Cycle risk](/kurser/rk-05-cykelrisk) in factory clothing: earnings live in the gas bill, not the factory.

## The marginal-cost price — who sets the price of an identical molecule

When the product is identical, price is set by the supply ladder: the most expensive factory needed. The course's example: with other variable costs of 150 dollars per tonne, the high-cost partner's total cost (gas 12) is 396 + 150 = 546; the low-cost producer's (gas 4), 132 + 150 = 282. At a world price of 560 the partner earns 560 − 546 = 14 dollars per tonne, the low-cost producer 560 − 282 = 278 — quotient 278 ÷ 14 = 19.9: nineteen times the difference, pure gas geography. Fall the price to 500: the partner's margin becomes 500 − 546 = minus 46 per tonne — the plant closes, capacity leaves, price stabilizes at the next partner's marginal cost: gas 8 gives cost 264 + 150 = 414, margin 500 − 414 = 86. The low-cost producer lives through it at 500 − 282 = 218. The fertilizer cycle shows in Nutrien: net income fell from 7,660 million dollars 2022 to 1,410 and 744, recovering to 2,153 — profit belongs to the ladder, not the know-how. The method — who sets the price, who owns the bottleneck, where the cycle stands — is [sector analysis's three questions](/kurser/se-16-sektoranalysens-metod); the commodity clock belongs to [the materials cycle guide](/blogg/ravarubolag-materialbranschens-cykel); phosphorus, mined rather than manufactured, borders on [the mining and metals course](/kurser/se-20-gruv-och-metallsektorn).

## R&D and the formula — the specialty moat

Specialty has no supply ladder to read: once a carmaker has qualified a surface treatment, or a pharmaceutical factory an excipient, switching means requalification — tests, certification, risk in the customer's production — and prices stay within a band, floored by [switching costs](/kurser/mt-05-byteskostnader-och-inlasning). R&D carries the field: Norden Special spends 150 million of 3,000 on development — 5 percent of revenue — against Norden Bulk's 60 of 12,000: half a percent, a tenth. The universe shows what formulas carry: Shin-Etsu, the world's largest silicon producer (wafers and silicones), carries gross margin 36.93, operating margin 19.18, revenue rising from 2,338 to 2,912 billion yen, net income from 437 to 648 four years in a row, interest coverage 53.67. Air Liquide, industrial gas on take-or-pay contracts, carries the sector's highest gross margin, 64.59: revenue stands still — 23,335 million euros in 2021 against 26,940 in 2025 — while net income rises from 2,572 to 3,518. Earnings growth begins in the margins — 53.85 to 64.18 — not in volume.

## The weight of plant capital — operating leverage

A nitrogen factory is steel, pressure vessels and furnaces — depreciated over decades, expensive to start and stop: temperature swings wear the equipment. Fixed costs magnify every move — [the margin ladder and operating leverage](/kurser/ln-03-marginaltrappan-och-operativ-havstavng) in chemistry's variant. The course's gas shock in pure form: gas at 4 rises to 8 — total cost from 282 to 414 dollars per tonne, the margin at unchanged price 560 from 278 to 146: nearly halved profitability, nothing happening to the factory. BASF, Germany's chemical giant, shows the weight: revenue fell from 87,327 million euros 2022 to 68,902, 61,444 and 59,657 — minus 31.7 percent in three years — earnings from minus 627 to 225, 1,298 and 1,619 million. The descent became a 2022 loss; recovery required balance-sheet protection — interest coverage 3.18, [solvency and interest coverage](/kurser/st-01-soliditet-och-rantetackning) the reader's second page.

## Paint, housing and the cycle — specialty against the housing market

Specialty's nearest volume border is paint: refined chemistry sold by the litre to construction and homeowners, demand following [the housing market's mechanics](/kurser/ma-08-bostadsmarknadens-mekanik) — construction, renovation, stock age. Sherwin-Williams, the largest US paint company, carries the contrast: gross margin rose through the inflation years from 42.8 to 48.9 percent, spread only 6.75 — price increases moved faster than raw-material cost, [pricing power](/kurser/mt-07-prisfullmakten) measured in the report. The dividend has risen 49 years in a row — 3.20 dollars per share, 1.00 percent yield — [dividend basics](/blogg/utdelningar-101). But the balance sheet shows the return on equity is partly leverage's algebra: 65.12 percent on equity against 16.39 invested, debt to equity 3.90 — read both measures, or neither.

## Valuation — the multiple follows the suit

The multiple map follows the margins' origin. In the universe, bulk's Yara trades at P/E 8.3, Nutrien 17.28; specialty's Sherwin-Williams 29.61, Air Liquide 29.36; Shin-Etsu between at 13.42; BASF, wearing both suits, 22.13. The pattern: bulk's E is a gas cycle the market rarely pays top earnings for; specialty's E rests on formulas that keep margins through the cycle. That is why [normalized multiples](/kurser/vr-02-normaliserade-multipler) and [the P/E's warnings](/kurser/km-009-pe) are standard tools: bulk's low multiple at the cycle's top is the classic trap — earnings belong to the cycle, not the company — comparison against [sector medians](/blogg/branschmedianer-akm2) within the family.

## Checklist: seven questions when you analyze chemical stocks

1. **The suit** — bulk or specialty? It decides how every line is read.
2. **The energy units** — how many per tonne (ammonia's 33), and what happens to the margin if gas doubles?
3. **The marginal-cost partner** — what total cost does the world's most expensive needed factory carry, where does price stand?
4. **The resource geography** — nitrogen at the gas field, phosphorus in the rock: where is the bottleneck, who owns it?
5. **The R&D share** — 5 percent of revenue is specialty, half a percent bulk: where does the formula carry profitability?
6. **The margin band** — 12 to 18 against 25 to 40: which part of the report belongs where?
7. **The cycle indicator** — agricultural prices, fertilizer inventories, capacity closures: where in the ladder is the market?

Chemical stocks reward the reader who first asks which of the two economies a report belongs to — then counts the gas bill against the supply ladder, not the cover label. The whole method: [the complete guide to Swedish stock analysis](/blogg/komplett-guide-svensk-aktieanalys-2026).
